+#!/bin/sh
+set -e
+
+SLEEP_COMMAND="sleep 567.555555"
+
+# Cleanup: kill any long-running process we started
+cleanup() {
+	# order matters to avoid restarting
+	[ -n "$keeper_pid" ] && kill "$keeper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+	[ -n "$sleep_pid_1" ] && kill "$sleep_pid_1" 2>/dev/null || true
+	[ -n "$sleep_pid_2" ] && kill "$sleep_pid_2" 2>/dev/null || true
+	pkill -u "$(id -un)" -f "^${SLEEP_COMMAND}$" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+# Setup: start a sleep with keep-one-running
+keep-one-running $SLEEP_COMMAND &
+keeper_pid=$!
+
+# Setup: wait until the first child sleep is running
+for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
+	sleep_pid_1=$(pgrep -u "$(id -un)" -f "^${SLEEP_COMMAND}$" || true)
+	[ -n "$sleep_pid_1" ] && break
+	sleep 1
+done
+
+# Test: the sleep is actually running
+if [ -z "$sleep_pid_1" ]; then
+	echo "FAIL: keep-one-running never started the command" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: keep-one-running started the sleep"
+
+# Test: we can not start the same command with run-one while it holds the lock
+if run-one $SLEEP_COMMAND; then
+	echo "FAIL: run-one was not blocked" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: concurrent run-one was blocked as expected"
+
+# Setup: kill the first sleep
+kill -9 "$sleep_pid_1"
+
+# Setup: wait for a new sleep to appear
+for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
+	sleep_pid_2=$(pgrep -u "$(id -un)" -f "^${SLEEP_COMMAND}$" | grep -v -e "^${sleep_pid_1}$" || true)
+	[ -n "$sleep_pid_2" ] && break
+	sleep 1
+done
+
+# Test: a new sleep is running
+if [ -z "$sleep_pid_2" ]; then
+	echo "FAIL: keep-one-running did not respawn the sleep" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: keep-one-running respawned the sleep"
+
+# Test: a different command is allowed to run
+run-one sleep 0.234567891
+echo "PASS: a different run-one command was allowed"

+#!/bin/sh
+set -e
+
+SLEEP_COMMAND="sleep 456.123456789"
+
+# Cleanup: kill any long-running process we started
+cleanup() {
+	[ -n "$main_pid" ] && kill "$main_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+	pkill -u "$(id -un)" -f "^${SLEEP_COMMAND}$" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+# Setup: start a sleep command (and save the pid for cleanup)
+run-one $SLEEP_COMMAND &
+main_pid=$!
+
+# Setup: wait until the first sleep acquires the lock and starts
+for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
+	pgrep -u "$(id -un)" -f "sleep 456.123456789" >/dev/null && break
+	sleep 1
+done
+
+# Test: we can not start the same sleep command twice
+if run-one $SLEEP_COMMAND; then
+	echo "FAIL: second run-one succeeded; expected it to be blocked" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: second run-one was blocked as expected"
+
+# Test: we can start a different sleep command
+run-one sleep 0.123456789
+echo "PASS: different run-one command was allowed"

+#!/bin/sh
+# Test that run-one-until-failure stops looping once the command fails.
+set -e
+
+HELPER="./helper-flakey"
+
+# Setup: generate the flakey helper script
+cat > "$HELPER" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/sh
+set -e
+cat exit_code.txt >> helper.txt
+exit "$(tail -n 1 helper.txt)"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$HELPER"
+
+# Cleanup: kill the runner (and its descendants) and remove scratch files
+cleanup() {
+	[ -n "$run_pid" ] && kill "$run_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+	pkill -u "$(id -un)" -f "run-one-until-failure ${HELPER}" 2>/dev/null || true
+	rm -f ./helper.txt ./exit_code.txt "$HELPER"
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+# Setup: make sure that there are no old logs present
+rm -rf ./helper.txt
+
+# Setup: make the helper script succeed
+echo 0 > exit_code.txt
+
+# Setup: start run-one-until-failure in the background
+timeout 600 run-one-until-failure "$HELPER" &
+run_pid=$!
+
+# Setup: give time for 5 runs
+for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
+	[ -f helper.txt ] && [ "$(grep -c . helper.txt)" -ge 5 ] && break
+	sleep 1
+done
+
+# Test: check that the helper run at least 5 times
+if [ "$(grep -c 0 helper.txt)" -lt 5 ]; then
+	echo "FAIL: helper was not restarted at least 5 times" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: helper was restarted at least 5 times"
+
+# Setup: make the helper exit with a failure
+echo 1 > exit_code.txt
+
+# Test: run-one-until-failure stopped looping (did not time out)
+rc=0
+wait "$run_pid" || rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -eq 124 ]; then
+	echo "FAIL: run-one-until-failure timed out" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: run-one-until-failure stopped looping"
+
+# Test: there was exactly one failed run
+if [ "$(grep -c 1 helper.txt)" -ne 1 ]; then
+	echo "FAIL: expected exactly one failed run" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: there was exactly one failed run"

diff --git a/debian/tests/cmd-run-this-one b/debian/tests/cmd-run-this-one
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..d114dd8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/tests/cmd-run-this-one
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+#!/bin/sh
+set -e
+
+SLEEP_COMMAND="sleep 345.987654321"
+
+# Cleanup: kill any long-running process we started
+cleanup() {
+	[ -n "$sleep_pid_1" ] && kill "$sleep_pid_1" 2>/dev/null || true
+	[ -n "$runone_pid" ] && kill "$runone_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+	[ -n "$runthisone_pid" ] && kill "$runthisone_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+	pkill -u "$(id -un)" -f "^${SLEEP_COMMAND}$" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+# Setup: start a simple sleep
+$SLEEP_COMMAND &
+sleep_pid_1=$!
+
+# Setup: start a sleep with run-one
+run-one $SLEEP_COMMAND &
+runone_pid=$!
+
+# Setup: wait until the second sleep is also running
+for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
+	sleep_pid_2=$(pgrep -u "$(id -un)" -f "^${SLEEP_COMMAND}$" | grep -v -e "^${sleep_pid_1}$"|| true)
+	[ -n "$sleep_pid_2" ] && break
+	sleep 1
+done
+
+# Setup: start a new sleep with run-this-one
+run-this-one $SLEEP_COMMAND &
+runthisone_pid=$!
+
+# Setup: wait until run-this-one's sleep starts.
+for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
+	sleep_pid_3=$(pgrep -u "$(id -un)" -f "^${SLEEP_COMMAND}$" | grep -v -e "^${sleep_pid_1}$" -e "^${sleep_pid_2}$" || true)
+	[ -n "$sleep_pid_3" ] && break
+	sleep 1
+done
+
+## Test: first sleep was killed
+if kill -0 "$sleep_pid_1" 2>/dev/null; then
+	echo "FAIL: first sleep is still alive" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: first sleep was killed"
+
+## Test: first sleep was killed
+if kill -0 "$sleep_pid_2" 2>/dev/null; then
+	echo "FAIL: second sleep is still alive" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: second sleep was killed"
+
+# Test: the third sleep from run-this-one is alive
+if [ -z "$sleep_pid_3" ] || ! kill -0 "$sleep_pid_3" 2>/dev/null; then
+	echo "FAIL: no live sleep found after run-this-one" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: the run-this-one sleep is alive"
+
+# Test: exactly one SLEEP_COMMAND process remains (originals were not just restarted)
+count=$(pgrep -u "$(id -un)" -f "^${SLEEP_COMMAND}$" | wc -l)
+if [ "$count" -ne 1 ]; then
+	echo "FAIL: expected exactly one '$SLEEP_COMMAND', found $count" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: exactly one sleep remains"
+
+# Test: a different command does not kill the original
+run-this-one sleep 0.987654321
+if ! kill -0 "$sleep_pid_3" 2>/dev/null; then
+	echo "FAIL: a different command killed the original sleep" 1>&2
+	exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: a different command left the original alive"
